story: Time is an illusion, Unix time doubly so
text: CuriousMarc has an excellent episode on an atomic clock. [VIDEO] I like to pretend I can fix computers, this guy can actually fix computers, which is probably why I find his show so fascinating.
If you want to see how an actual application of this works, I've yet to see a description better than in CuriousMarc's HP 5061A series: [VIDEO]

CuriousMarc made a video last week where he uses a vintage HP 5061A atomic clock and explains how it works. It's interesting to see that atomic clocks aren't just some giant laboratory thing, but a product you could buy, even in the 1960s. [VIDEO]

text: CuriousMarc uploaded a video to Youtube showing the startup procedure for an HP 5061A cesium clock [0]. They switch on the clock and compare it to a GPS reference. Seeing the abstract description realized in concrete terms through hot cesium tubes, phase locked loops, and Lissajous curves was really fascinating. [0] [VIDEO]
